toc.title: Regulations, AWS governance services, data governance, processes and practice

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Identify the AWS services that support governance and compliance: Config, Inspector, Artifact, CloudTrail and Trusted Advisor
  • Describe data governance strategies: lifecycles, logging, residency, monitoring and retention
  • Describe governance processes: policies, review cadence, frameworks such as the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix, transparency standards and training

2Regulations, AWS governance services, data governance, processes and practice

Running case

Cedar and Salt Meets the Auditors

  • Auditors ask for proof of compliance for the booking assistant
  • Questions: what rules apply, what is configured, who did what, and how long do we keep guest data?
  • Leaders want a repeatable review, not a one-time check
  • Your job: choose the services and processes

The Regulatory Landscape and AWS Compliance [Verify live]

  • AI-specific rules and frameworks: the EU AI Act and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) AI Risk Management Framework
  • Data protection laws: GDPR, CCPA and CPRA; industry rules: HIPAA for health, APRA for finance
  • Cross-border data needs data sovereignty controls
  • AWS has an accredited ISO/IEC 42001 certification for AI services; the certificate lists the covered services and is in AWS Artifact
  • AWS's certification does not make your application compliant: you still must comply
  • As of 5 November 2026: check AWS compliance pages for current scope

Exam tip: AWS provides compliant infrastructure; you prove your own application complies.

AWS Config and Amazon Inspector

Service What it does Governance use
AWS Config Records how resources are configured and how they changed; evaluates them with rules and conformance packs Show that settings follow policy, such as encrypted buckets; keep configuration history for audits
Amazon Inspector Continuously scans EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and network exposure Find and fix weaknesses in the workloads that run your AI application

Exam tip: Configuration history and rules: AWS Config. Vulnerability scanning: Amazon Inspector.

AWS Artifact, AWS CloudTrail and AWS Trusted Advisor [Verify live]

Service What it does
AWS Artifact On-demand AWS compliance reports (SOC, ISO, PCI) and online agreements
AWS CloudTrail Records who did what, when, as events; 90 days of event history free, trails to S3, CloudTrail Lake for longer retention
AWS Trusted Advisor Checks your environment against best practices and recommends fixes
  • As of 5 November 2026: the full set of Trusted Advisor checks needs a paid support plan; plan names are changing

Exam tip: Reports for auditors: Artifact. Activity history: CloudTrail. Best-practice checks: Trusted Advisor.

Data Governance Strategies

Strategy What to do
Data lifecycle Define how data is collected, used, archived and deleted
Logging Keep audit trails of data access and model interactions
Residency Keep data in approved Regions, and control cross-border use
Monitoring and observation Watch data use, quality and drift with alerts
Retention Keep records as long as the rules require, and no longer

Exam tip: Name the data question first: how long, where, who, and what changed.

AWS Services for Data Governance [Verify live]

  • AWS Lake Formation: one place for fine-grained access control to data lakes, down to columns, rows and cells, with audit logs in CloudTrail
  • Amazon S3 Glacier storage classes: low-cost long-term archives for data you must retain; S3 lifecycle rules move data between classes
  • Amazon Bedrock data retention: you control whether prompts and outputs are retained, per Region, with modes such as none, default and AWS review
  • Region choice keeps data resident where the rules require
  • As of 5 November 2026: retention modes apply to specific models; check the model's terms

Exam tip: Data lake permissions: Lake Formation. Cheap long-term retention: S3 Glacier.

Governance Processes

Process What it involves
Policies Written rules for acceptable AI use, data and risk limits
Review cadence Regular reviews and updates, not a one-time approval
Review strategies A multidisciplinary team: legal, security, ethics, business and technical; an AI risk register; audits
Transparency standards Disclose AI use and document models and data
Team training People learn the policies, risks and responsible use

Exam tip: Governance is a cycle of policy, review, audit and training.

The Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix

  • Scope 1: use a public generative AI service
  • Scope 2: use an enterprise application with embedded generative AI
  • Scope 3: build on a pre-trained model through an API
  • Scope 4: fine-tune a model with your data
  • Scope 5: train a model from scratch
  • Five disciplines: governance and compliance, legal and privacy, risk management, controls, resilience

Exam tip: The more you own of the model and data, the more governance work falls to you.

What the Exam Asks: Governance and Compliance

  • Which service: Config, Inspector, Artifact, CloudTrail or Trusted Advisor
  • Which data strategy: lifecycle, logging, residency, monitoring or retention
  • Which process: policies, review cadence, review strategy, transparency standard or training
  • Which framework: the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix, and which scope
  • Which regulation: EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, GDPR, HIPAA, ISO/IEC 42001

Exam tip: Name the need first: report, history, scan, configuration or rule.

Design Check: Cedar and Salt Meets the Auditors

What the auditors ask Name and answer
A copy of AWS's ISO and SOC reports AWS Artifact
Who called the model APIs, and when AWS CloudTrail
Proof that buckets stay encrypted, with history AWS Config rules
Are our compute workloads free of known vulnerabilities? Amazon Inspector
Quick best-practice check of the account AWS Trusted Advisor
Column-level access to guest data in the data lake AWS Lake Formation
Keep old logs for years cheaply S3 Glacier classes
Booking app uses a third-party model through an API Scope 3 of the scoping matrix
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

3Exam Q&A

3.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Which AWS service provides on-demand downloads of AWS compliance reports, such as SOC and ISO reports?

  • AAWS Artifact
  • BAWS Config
  • CAmazon Inspector
  • DAWS Trusted Advisor
Show the answer

Answer: A. AWS Artifact gives on-demand access to AWS security and compliance documents and agreements. Config records configurations, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, and Trusted Advisor checks best practices.

S2Cedar and Salt must show auditors who called its Amazon Bedrock APIs and when. Which service records this activity?

  • AAWS Config
  • BAmazon Inspector
  • CAWS CloudTrail
  • DAWS Artifact
Show the answer

Answer: C. CloudTrail records actions taken by a user, role or AWS service as events, so you can see who did what and when. Config tracks resource configuration, Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, and Artifact provides reports.

S3Which TWO statements about AWS Config and Amazon Inspector are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • AConfig records resource configurations and evaluates them against rules
  • BInspector records every API call made by users and roles
  • CInspector scans workloads for vulnerabilities and network exposure
  • DConfig reviews model prompts for toxic content
  • EConfig scans application source code for software flaws
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Config records and evaluates resource configuration; Inspector continuously scans EC2 instances, container images and Lambda functions for vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. API activity is CloudTrail, and toxic content is handled by Guardrails.

S4Cedar and Salt builds its assistant on a third-party pre-trained foundation model through an API. Which scope of the Generative AI Security Scoping Matrix fits?

  • AScope 1, a consumer app
  • BScope 3, pre-trained models
  • CScope 4, fine-tuned models
  • DScope 5, self-trained models
Show the answer

Answer: B. Scope 3 is building your own application on an existing third-party foundation model through an API. Scope 4 refines a model with your data, and Scope 5 trains a model from scratch.

S5Which approach best supports governance of an AI system over time?

  • AA single approval at launch, and then no changes
  • BLetting each team set its own rules, and never reviewing
  • CA written policy, kept by one person, with no training
  • DRegular reviews, an AI risk register, audits and team training
Show the answer

Answer: D. Governance is a repeating cycle: policies, a review cadence, audits, a risk register, transparency standards and team training. A one-time approval or untrained, unreviewed rules do not keep pace with change.
